payload.summary: Production deploys stopped landing for 27 hours on 2026-09-21; likely cause Railway Wait for CI skipping deploys while main CI was red
payload.detail: UPDATE 2026-10-21 (read-only GitHub deployment statuses and Actions run times; no Railway access): LIKELY CAUSE FOUND, and it is not a healthcheck rollback. Each of the four stuck production deploys went from in_progress to inactive within 5 to 6 seconds of that commit's CI workflow run on main concluding failure: ef257fa5c CI failed 10:12:32Z, deploy inactive 10:12:37Z; f44ae5397 10:31:12Z / 10:31:18Z; 56b123509 16:48:48Z / 16:48:54Z; 373046b76 17:36:52Z / 17:36:58Z. That is Railway's documented Wait for CI behaviour (a failed workflow run skips the deploy at once; docs/deployment-architecture.md). 3a43f808d, which triggered no CI run, deployed normally. 76bf29ffa began deploying at 09:08Z on 2026-09-22, three minutes before its own CI run failed at 09:11Z, which fits a manual deploy or Wait for CI being switched off then. So the stall was Wait for CI enabled on the production service while CI on main was red (release-browser-matrix Firefox/WebKit, Lighthouse and PR required failures). By 2026-09-27 the setting read source.checkSuites false. The same signature recurs on 2026-10-21: 3b4518fdb went inactive at 07:10:45Z, seven seconds after its Docker image build run failed at 07:10:38Z, so Wait for CI appears to be on again and any red workflow run on a main commit skips the production deploy (handed to the Alert root causes work, #3685). Next action, owner: read the Wait for CI setting on the Railway app and worker services and confirm; then decide per #HYSWAF whether it stays on, which requires main CI to stay green. PRIOR DETAIL: Second occurrence of the Railway deploy-rollback failure mode first seen 2026-09-11..09-14 (24 consecutive rollbacks, documented in scripts/check-live-deployment-freshness.mjs and docs/deployment-architecture.md 'Readiness: what /api/health/ready may and may not ask'). Measured 2026-09-22 from GitHub deployment statuses: the Database service in the production environment last landed a deploy at 2026-09-21T05:59Z (3a43f808d) and did not land another until 2026-09-22T09:15Z (76bf29ffa, PR #2978). In between, four production deployments were created for ef257fa5c, f44ae5397, 56b123509 and 373046b76 and every one went in_progress -> inactive without ever reaching success. All four built cleanly in the Docker image build workflow, live-drift was green on the 2026-09-21 migrations, and Railway built PR preview environments normally throughout, so the integration, the image and the database are all ruled out. That leaves Railway-side deploy/start/healthcheck rejection, which is the documented mechanism: each healthcheck attempt gets ~10s against /api/health/ready and a container that cannot answer inside the window is discarded and rolled back, leaving the previous deploy serving. Confirming which of the four failed and why needs the Railway deployment logs for the production environment, which no agent session has had access to. Production recovered on its own and no fix was applied, so the trigger is unknown and can recur. Separately confirmed NOT a fault: nine main commits in the same window got a staging deploy but no production deploy at all - all nine touched no path matched by watchPatterns in railway.app.json, which is correct filtering. Alerting clarification (rewrites a false claim in the original draft of this request): live-domain-monitor.yml already has monitor-routing (issues: write + actions/github-script) as of #2884 / ledger #TN512M, and it DID fire during this stall — pinned issue #2973 ('Live domain monitor failing', label live-monitor-failure) was opened 2026-09-21T12:40Z, updated on later red runs including the deployment-freshness failure at 2026-09-22T06:47Z, and closed on the next green run at 2026-09-22T12:41Z. So 'nothing routes a red monitor run' is false. What remains unverified for human delivery: despite #2973 being open and repeatedly commented for ~24 hours of the stall, the gap was still found only because a human inspected GitHub deployment statuses, not because anyone acted on the pinned issue. That matches the #TN512M residual ('Close once a genuine outage has produced a notification someone acted on') and the workflow comment that owner failure emails arrive unread. Durable next actions: (1) pull Railway production deployment logs for the four inactive deploys and record the reject reason; (2) treat this stall as the missing #TN512M real-outage evidence that GitHub-issue routing alone is insufficient delivery, and decide a human-reachable path (page/Slack/owner push) before adding more probes. Pairs with #HYSWAF (Railway deploys every main push without waiting for required checks) and #TN512M.
